dossier.public_summary: The 0.799-day dip repeats exactly at the star’s 0.80-day spot rotation period with a large out-of-transit swing almost as big as the dip itself and a depth that changes by ~54% between sectors. This is the pattern of stellar spots/variability on an active M dwarf, not a small planet transit.

reasons.why: Phase-curve amplitude is 4695 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.8954, chi2 314.4, dof 9) essentially as large as the 5243 ppm transit depth. Positively favours a close stellar companion over a planet.

rotation measures rotation_d 0.8005 vs signal_period_d 0.798761 (signal_at_rotation_multiple 1) with huge false alarms 1.412e-137 and 3.195e-233 and amplitudes 17434 / 13885 ppm. Signal is exactly the spot rotation period, not a transit period.

Sector depths differ 53.63% (sectors p_constant 7.909e-8, chi2 28.83 dof 1: 6961 +/-416 ppm vs 4017 +/-356 ppm). sector_depths_by_source verdict is changes_within_a_source, so the depth really changes, as expected for spot modulation tied to rotation, not a stable planet.

Centroid is on_target (offset 3.375 arcsec err 1.689 sigma 1.998) so dip is on the target M dwarf (Teff 3340 K Rad 0.3825). A spotted equal-area signal of the same period explains the dip without a neighbour.

Flat-bottom shape does not outweigh the above. A blended binary can also be flat-bottomed and size rp_rearth 3.03 alone is not evidence for a planet when period, depth change and phase curve show stellar variability.
